generalfeedback.text:
Worked solution

We recall the following derivations of functions

Functions Derivative formulas
\( \sqrt{f} \) \(\displaystyle \frac{f'}{2f}\)
\( \ln f\) \( \displaystyle \frac{f'}{f} \)
\((f + g)' \) \(f' + g'\)
\(\displaystyle \frac{f}{g} \) \(\displaystyle \frac{f'g - g'f}{g^2} \)
\(\alpha f\) \(\alpha f'\)

(a) \(z= \displaystyle {@f_1@}\)

Let’s start with finding \( \partial_{u} z\). We first differentiate with respect to \(x\).

\( \begin{align} \displaystyle \partial_{u} z & = \displaystyle \frac{ \partial_{u} ({@f_numerator@}) \cdot ({@f_denominator@})-\partial_{u} ({@f_denominator@}) \cdot ({@f_numerator@})}{({@f_denominator@})^2} \\ & = {@ta_1@} \end{align} \)

Next let’s start with finding \(\displaystyle \frac{\partial z}{\partial v} \). We differentiate with respect to \(v\).

\( \begin{align} \displaystyle \partial_{v} z & = \displaystyle \frac{ \partial_{v} ({@f_numerator@}) \cdot ({@f_denominator@})-\partial_{v} ({@f_denominator@}) \cdot ({@f_numerator@})}{({@f_denominator@})^2} \\ & = {@ta_2@} \end{align} \)

(b) \(g(x, y, z)= \displaystyle {@g_xyz@}\)

Let’s start with finding \( \displaystyle \partial_{x} g\). We first differentiate with respect to \(x\).

\( \begin{align} \displaystyle \partial_{x} g & = \displaystyle \frac{ \partial_{x} ({@g_numerator@}) \cdot ({@g_denominator@})-\partial_{x} ({@g_denominator@}) \cdot ({@g_numerator@})}{({@g_denominator@})^2} \\ & = {@ta_3@} \end{align} \)

Next let’s start with finding \(\displaystyle \partial_{y} g\). We differentiate with respect to \(y\).

\( \begin{align} \displaystyle \partial_{y} g & = \frac{ \partial_{y} ({@g_numerator@}) \cdot ({@g_denominator@})-\partial_{y} ({@g_denominator@}) \cdot ({@g_numerator@})}{({@g_denominator@})^2} \\ & = {@ta_4@} \end{align} \)

Finally we differentiate \(g\) with respect to \(z\).

\( \begin{align} \displaystyle \partial_{z} g & = \frac{ \partial_{z} ({@g_numerator@}) \cdot ({@g_denominator@})-\partial_{z} ({@g_denominator@}) \cdot ({@g_numerator@})}{({@g_denominator@})^2} \\ & = {@ta_5@} \end{align} \)

(c) \(h(x,y)=\displaystyle{@h@}\)

Let’s start with finding \( \partial_{x} h\). We first differentiate with respect to \(x\).

\( \begin{align} \displaystyle \partial_{x} h & = {@(1/2)@} \cdot \left[{@fxy@}\right]^{@(-1/2)@} \cdot \partial_{x} \left({@fxy@} \right) \\ \displaystyle & = {@(1/2)@} \cdot \left[{@fxy@}\right]^{@(-1/2)@} \cdot \left[ \partial_{x} ({@aa*x^2@}) + \frac{\partial_{x} \left({@bb*x-cc*y^2@}\right) }{{@bb*x-cc*y^2@}} \right] \\ & = {@(1/2)@} \cdot \left[{@fxy@}\right]^{@(-1/2)@} \cdot \left[ \partial_{x} ({@aa*x^2@}) + \frac{\partial_{x} ({@bb*x@})-\partial_{x} ({@cc*y^2@})}{{@bb*x-cc*y^2@}} \right] \\ & = {@(1/2)@} \cdot \left[{@fxy@}\right]^{@(-1/2)@} \cdot \left[ {@diff(aa*x^2,x)@} + \frac{{@diff(bb*x-cc*y^2,x)@}}{{@bb*x-cc*y^2@}} \right] \\ & = {@ta_6@} \end{align} \)

Let’s start with finding \(\displaystyle \partial_{y} h\). We differentiate with respect to \(y\).

\( \begin{align} \displaystyle \partial_{y} h & = {@(1/2)@} \cdot \left[{@fxy@}\right]^{@(-1/2)@} \cdot \partial_{y} \left({@fxy@} \right) \\ \displaystyle & = {@(1/2)@} \cdot \left[{@fxy@}\right]^{@(-1/2)@} \cdot \left[ \partial_{y} ({@aa*x^2@}) + \displaystyle \frac{\partial_{y} \left({@bb*x-cc*y^2@}\right) }{{@bb*x-cc*y^2@}} \right] \\ & = \displaystyle {@(1/2)@} \cdot \left[{@fxy@}\right]^{@(-1/2)@} \cdot \left[ \partial_{y} ({@aa*x^2@}) + \displaystyle \frac{\partial_{y} ({@bb*x@})-\partial_{y} ({@cc*y^2@})}{{@bb*x-cc*y^2@}} \right] \\ & = {@(1/2)@} \cdot \left[{@fxy@}\right]^{@(-1/2)@} \cdot \left[ {@diff(aa*x^2,y)@} + \frac{{@diff(bb*x-cc*y^2,y)@}}{{@bb*x-cc*y^2@}} \right] \\ & = {@ta_7@} \end{align} \)
